originality.rationale: The inspected motivating full text bounds the logarithmic extinction rate and develops endemic stationary Gaussian sensitivity, but neither proves the exact subcritical exponent nor gives a time-asymptotic Gaussian law and sharp noise-correlation floor for the log of infected abundance. Directly relevant general epidemic CLTs concern large-population scaling rather than large-time scaling for this multiplicative environmental SDE. Database and prior-claim comparison found no implication covering the combined theorem; an unindexed equivalent remains a declared risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or unpublished source-specific logarithmic central limit theorems might overlap the claim.
Some other stochastic SIRS numerical or CLT papers have incomplete indexed full-text coverage; absence in searches is not proof of novelty.
The correlated-Brownian statement is an extension of the originally independent-driver model, though the motivating source explicitly discusses correlated drivers in Remark 3.2.

value.rationale: The source 2026 threshold gives only an asymptotic sign and an upper growth-rate bound, insufficient for uncertainty of low-level infection. The exact log-abundance CLT supplies a biologically interpretable quantitative uncertainty measure that depends explicitly on cross-class forcing. The attainable anticorrelation floor is a structural obstruction to noise cancellation. It is not an arbitrary parameter slice, elementary zero check, or recomputation of existing endemic Gaussian plots; there is a motivated dynamical and statistical observable whose behavior is new relative to inspected sources.
